findings.reason: Untrusted source: dn_process_ack is reached from dn_nsp_backlog_rcv (dn_nsp_in.c:876) on remotely received NSP frames registered via the ETH_P_DNA_RT packet_type dn_route_rcv (af_decnet.c:2107); skb->len and the ack words are attacker-chosen. Violated invariant: the only presence guarantee is skb->len < 2 checks on total length; skb_pull() validates solely against skb->len (bytes in frags/fraglist included) and never linearizes, so ptr (=skb->data saved at line 130, advanced at 139) is dereferenced as 16-bit words at lines 137 and 151 without any check that those bytes are in the linear head. Unsafe use: le16_to_cpu(*ptr) reads 2 bytes past skb_headlen when the ack words sit in frags. Counterevidence checked: dn_nsp_rx_packet linearizes at dn_nsp_in.c:790-793 but only 'if (cb->nsp_flags & ~0x60)', i.e. data segments (flags & 0x60, including the data/ack frames that reach dn_process_ack via the else branch at 856-876) are explicitly exempt, and no pskb_may_pull/skb_linearize exists between there and the reads; the s05 pskb_may_pull calls at 718/748/761/764 cover at most 5 bytes and predate the exempt-branch decision, so bytes beyond the header remain unguaranteed for data segments.
findings.conclusion: dn_process_ack reads 16-bit ack words through a pointer saved from skb->data after unchecked skb_pull(2) with only skb->len checks, so a non-linear NSP data frame (exempt from skb_linearize) makes *ptr read past the linear head: remote linear-area OOB read (needs CONFIG_DECNET).

findings.reason: Untrusted source: nfc_llcp_recv_agf is reached from nfc_llcp_rx_skb's LLCP_PDU_AGF case (llcp_core.c:1465) on frames delivered by the NFC LLCP MAC layer, whose contents (AGF PDU lengths) are peer-controlled. Violated invariant: the loop guards only on skb->len (total bytes incl. frags); skb_pull at 1374/1379/1403 is unchecked and never linearizes, so the two-byte length read at 1377 and the skb_put_data(new_skb, skb->data, pdu_len) copy at 1397 can address bytes that are not in the linear head. Unsafe use: 2-byte read and variable-length copy past skb_headlen on a frag-backed AGF frame. Counterevidence checked: no pskb_may_pull/skb_linearize anywhere in nfc_llcp_recv_agf; the pdu_len > skb->len bound at 1381 is again a total-length bound, not a linear-head bound; residual uncertainty is whether an NFC digital/nci path can actually deliver a non-linear skb here (not traced in this session).
findings.conclusion: nfc_llcp_recv_agf uses unchecked skb_pull as a linearizer: the skb->data[0]<<8|data[1] length read and the pdu_len copy take bytes that skb->len but not skb_headlen guarantees, an OOB read of the linear head on non-linear AGF frames (needs CONFIG_NFC + non-linear RX skb).

candidates.reason: dn_access_copy (1001-1018) pulls and memcpys attacker-supplied length bytes unchecked, but the reachable path (dn_nsp_conn_init -> sk_receive_queue -> dn_accept at af_decnet.c:1138) is pre-validated by dn_check_idf in dn_nsp_conn_init's parse (dn_nsp_in.c:296-310, max 39/16 with follow-on counted against len), so the copy lengths were already validated against the packet.
candidates.conclusion: Structural unchecked pull remains, but each length byte was validated by dn_check_idf before the copy, so no missing-linear-guarantee beyond the non-linearity question already covered by the dn_process_ack finding.

candidates.reason: lapb_decode reads skb->data[0]/[1] after skb_pull(1) at line 145, but pskb_may_pull(skb, 2) guards at lines 116, 149 and 162 precede every multi-byte read, and the remaining reads are single data[0] bytes inside the already-guaranteed 2 bytes.
candidates.conclusion: No unguarded post-pull dereference: all reads are within bytes pskb_may_pull already guaranteed.

candidates.reason: bpq_rcv's skb_pull(skb, 2) at 209 follows pskb_may_pull(sizeof(struct ethhdr)) at 182 and skb_cow(skb, sizeof(struct ethhdr)) at 204, so the length bytes read at 207 and the pull are inside the linear head; the skb is then re-parsed through ax25_type_trans.
candidates.conclusion: Linear head guaranteed by the preceding pskb_may_pull and skb_cow; not a pull-as-linearizer site.

candidates.reason: pptp_rcv_core's skb_pull(skb, headersize) at 314 and skb_pull(skb, 2) at 320 follow pskb_may_pull(skb, headersize + payload_len) at 301, so payload[0]/[1]/[4] reads at 307-316 are inside the linear head (the 3-byte len check at 318 covers the second pull).
candidates.conclusion: Explicit pskb_may_pull(headersize + payload_len) precedes the pull and the dependent reads.

candidates.reason: x25_state1_machine pulls X25_STD_MIN_LEN only after pskb_may_pull at 107; x25_parse_address_block (af_x25.c:91-105) and x25_parse_facilities (x25_facilities.c:60-66) each pskb_may_pull the exact bytes their later pulls consume.
candidates.conclusion: X.25 call-request path is pull-guarded at every step; no unchecked linearizer.

coverage_gaps: Non-linearity preconditions were assessed structurally (which subsystems linearize before parsing); no per-driver audit confirmed that a frag/fraglist-backed skb actually reaches dn_process_ack or nfc_llcp_recv_agf in any s05 configuration.

The 1160 pull-family call sites in net/ and drivers/net/ were machine-triaged to 103 post-pull-dereference candidates and then read selectively; wireless and USB RX helpers that surfaced in the scan (ath9k/ath10k/rtlwifi/mt76/mwifiex/lan78xx/smsc75xx etc.) parse skbs their own driver just built and were deprioritized without full per-function reads.
No runtime reproducer, KASAN build, or compilation was performed against this read-only snapshot, so both findings are source-reading hypotheses without empirical confirmation.
limitations: Both findings require a non-linear (frag- or fraglist-backed) skb at the parse point: DECnet additionally needs CONFIG_DECNET (legacy, off in most distro kernels) and the NFC one needs CONFIG_NFC plus an LLCP peer sending a crafted AGF PDU through a driver that does not linearize; if every delivering path builds linear skbs the code is fragile but not exploitable.

Because no pskb_may_pull ever runs inside dn_process_ack or nfc_llcp_recv_agf, the concrete failure mode is an out-of-bounds read of the linear head (bytes past skb_headlen, i.e. reading memory that belongs to frags) rather than the seed's pskb_may_pull-induced slab use-after-free; the branch treats both as the same missing-linear-guarantee invariant.

dn_process_ack is the branch's own prescribed open template, so it is reported as verified-in-place rather than as an independently discovered variant; net/phonet/pep.c pep_get_sb (present at s05 pep.c:45-66) was excluded per assignment rules and never reported.

The coarse scanner's heuristics (call line plus up to 10 following lines for dependent reads, back-scan for enclosing function) can misjoin multi-line calls or miss consumption in earlier lines, so a small number of false negatives among the 103 flagged sites cannot be excluded.
Snapshot revision is opaque (no git history permitted), so it cannot be determined whether upstream has since fixed either reported site; line numbers are valid only for this supplied s05 tree.
